newsitem.title: UK: UK retail prices rise yr/yr 2.6 pct in March.
newsitem.headline: UK retail prices rise yr/yr 2.6 pct in March.

text.p: The Office for National Statistics released the following March retail price indices.
RETAIL PRICES INDEX MARCH FEB MAR 96
Mth pct change ex MIPs, tax 0.3 0.4 0.5
COMPONENT DETAILS OF THE ALL-ITEMS INDEX (PCT CHANGES) -
NOTE - Consensus forecast was RPI +0.4 pct month-on-month and +2.7 pct YY, RPIX +2.8 pct YY, RPIY +2.5 pct YY.
* Lowest since May 1995, last lower in April 1995 when 2.6 pct.

** The 2.6 percent drop in seasonal food prices was the biggest for a March since 1957 when there was a drop of 3.4 percent. The anual drop of 15.6 percent was the greatest since May 1983 when there was a drop of 16.1.

The RPI all goods measure rose 2.0 percent yr-on-yr in March, down from 2.3 percent in February. The RPI for all services rose 3.3 percent yr-on-yr in March, unchanged from Feb. The ONS said the fall in the all-items 12 month rate was largely attributable to food prices, with both seasonable and non-seasonable food exerting considerable downward pressure.

Prices for some fresh vegetables, for example, lettuce and cucumbers, fell sharply over the month in contrast to the increases seen last March when poor weather conditions affected supplies of domestic and European produce.
There were small upward effects from fresh fruit and unprocessed potato prices.
Motoring costs also had a downward effect, mainly from prices of second hand motor vehicles which rose less this year than last March and from second hand motor bike prices which fell this month.
There was also a small downward effect from petrol prices, particularly unleaded and diesel fuel, where the decrease this March was much sharper than last year.

But there were upward effects on the 12-month rate from household goods prices where price increases and the full effects of recoveries in furniture and furnishings following record January sales exceeded those seen last March.

There were also small upward effects from electrical appliances and items of household equipment, as recoveries this month from special offers resulted in larger price increases from those a year earlier.

Clothing and footwear prices also boosted the 12 month rate with price rises in all clothing sectors exerting upward pressure because price rises were steeper than those a year ago. There were further recoveries from January's record sales, as well as price increases for many new season's items.
